products.name: WERK83 Porsche 917 LH Hippie Martini #3 Le Mans 1970
products.description:
Le Mans, June 1970. Porsche brought seven 917s and won for the first time; the red and white #23 of Attwood and Herrmann took the flag. Five laps behind it, in second, came this one - Martini Racing's only car, #3, driven by Gerard Larrousse and Willi Kauhsen, chassis 917-043, long tail, 4.5-litre flat twelve.

It is remembered less for the result than for the paint. The swirling violet and green pattern was applied at the circuit, and the story goes it was still wet when the car went out. Everybody called it the Hippie Porsche.

WERK83's model carries the full livery: the psychedelic swirls across the long tail body, the Martini, Shell, Bosch, CIBIE and Goodyear decals, the driver names on the cockpit, the #3 roundels on nose, doors and tail, and the twin filler caps on the rear deck. It sits on a black base with an engraved plate reading PORSCHE 917 LANG HECK 4.5 - Martini Racing 1970, and comes in the WERK83 display box. Static model, nothing opens.

products.name: KK Scale Porsche 911 (930) Turbo 3.0 1976
products.description:
The first of the Turbos, and the rarest. Between 1975 and 1977 Porsche built fewer than 3,000 of the 3.0-litre 930 - enough to homologate it for racing, not many more. It had no intercooler, 260 PS, and boost that arrived all at once: the reason the 930 picked up the nickname widowmaker before it was even a classic.

Everything that made the shape famous is here: the flared rear wings, the whale tail sitting up on the engine lid, black rubber bumper bellows instead of chrome, the narrow indicator lenses and the deep-dish alloys with black centres and polished rims. In white the arches and the black wheel-arch stone guards read more clearly than they do on a dark car.

KK Scale's model sits on a black display base with an engraved plate reading 911 (930) Turbo 3.0 1976, and carries a German plate reading S PT 1976. Sealed body - doors and bonnet do not open. Supplied in the KK Scale display box.

products.name: KK Scale Lamborghini Espada S2 1970
products.description:
A Lamborghini you can take three friends in. The Espada was Gandini's shape for Bertone - a front-engined V12 grand tourer with four proper seats, a long bonnet, and a glass tailgate that made it the most practical supercar of its day. The name is the sword a matador uses.

1970 brought the S2: revised grille, a new dash, and the 3.9-litre V12 wound up to around 350 hp. It is a big car - nearly 4.7 metres - and at 1:18 that length is the point: the low nose with its quad headlights, the twin bonnet vents, the slim chrome bumpers, the slatted rear screen under the glass, and that tapering tail.

KK Scale's model is finished in gold metallic with a tan interior, chrome hubcaps, and sits on a black display base with an engraved plate reading Espada S2 1970. Sealed body - doors and bonnet do not open. Supplied in the KK Scale display box.

products.name: Sun Star MG Metro 6R4 #1 Billy Coleman Donegal Rally 1986 Winner

Ireland, June 1986, and Billy Coleman put the new Metro 6R4 on the Donegal International Rally and won with it. It was his fourth Donegal victory, and his first in the Metro 6R4.

The 6R4 is the odd one of the Group B cars: no turbo, a 3.0-litre V6 sitting behind the driver, four-wheel drive, and that short wheelbase with the wide arches and the big rear wing. It sounds like nothing else of its era.

Sun Star's model is the #1 Donegal car, carrying Coleman and Morgan's names, the Rothmans-era livery, the deep front spoiler and the roof vents. Doors open on the model, and the rear bodywork lifts away to show the V6, the exhausts and the radiators behind it, with the roll cage and the carbon seats visible through the glass. Limited edition of 999 pieces worldwide.

products.name: NOREV Mercedes 190E 2.3-16 #11 Senna Race of Champions 1984
products.description:
Nurburgring, 12 May 1984. Mercedes-Benz had just rebuilt the Grand Prix circuit and had a new model to sell, so they put twenty identical 190 E 2.3-16s on the grid and invited the Formula 1 field to race them. Nine past world champions took the start. A 24-year-old Brazilian in car 11, in his first Formula 1 season, won.

The cars were production 2.3-16s with a roll cage and a racing seat and nothing else - the same engine, the same suspension, the same gearbox as the road car. Senna's win there is the one people point to when they explain how he arrived.

Norev's model is the #11 Race of Champions car in smoke silver, with the SENNA lettering on the doors and the screen, the 190 E 2.3-16 plates, the boot spoiler and the deep-dish alloys. Full openings: doors, bonnet and boot all open.
